brief: KOSPI closed down 7.6% overnight, breaking its longer-term trend line and trading below its 200-day moving average. The late-July selloff found support slightly below current levels, raising the question of whether that holds as KOSPI's last line of defense. KOSPI is at its most oversold level since October 2022. Volatility has flipped from the melt-up's unusual spot-up/vol-up pattern to spot crashing while volatility explodes higher, which the note calls pure panic. The KOSPI-versus-SOX performance gap is widening despite SOX's own decline, raising the question of whether Korea has overshot to the downside or US semis have yet to catch down. Taiwan, previously seen as immune to the regional selloff, is starting to roll over, and the note asks whether the Taiwan-Korea performance gap closes through Taiwan catching down or Korea catching up. With Taiwan's AI-trade positioning still at record levels and doubts growing around AI capex, inflation and Chinese competition, the note argues the longer-term AI story may stay intact but says crowded positioning and elevated expectations make tactical downside hedges attractive, and that the risk of a broader AI-trade unwind is rising.
